_what: Scenarios whose MEASURED turn (follow_ups[-1], else prompt) cannot reach their own tool through answerable_tools. Shrink-only. Almost every one is a DECLARATION gap: the sentence asks for what the tool does and the tool has not declared those words.
_three_categories_2026_08_30: This file used to be ONE flat list and it conflated three things that need OPPOSITE rules. Five of its 25 entries were already 'Yes, go ahead and do it.' confirmation turns — unreachable BY DESIGN, sitting in a shrink-only debt list they can never leave. Splitting them out was forced by two new scenarios of the same shape; it was not caused by them.
_scenarios_rule: DECLARATION DEBT. The sentence asks for what the tool does and the tool has not declared those words. SHRINK-ONLY: a new entry is a defect to fix (widen the tool's synonyms) or a decision to record, never a row to append. Becoming reachable is PROGRESS and the entry must be removed.

by_design.scenarios-c-siblingpick-adopt.json::glos: THE MEASURED TURN MUST NOT REACH THIS TOOL — that is the finding, not a gap. `tool_under_test` is glossary_adopt_standards because `--approvals allow-under-test` grants the DECLARED tool, and this arm has to grant the tool the model actually reaches for. The tool whose selection is being measured is glossary_propose_batch, and it IS reachable — measured 2026-08-30, answerable_tools returns exactly {glossary_propose_batch}. That is precisely D-SURFACING-IS-NECESSARY-BUT-NOT-SUFFICIENT's decisive case: the model passes over the only tool its own words select, in favour of one they do not match. Widening adopt_standards to match would DESTROY that measurement.
by_design.scenarios-c-kgedge-nodes.json::kg-propos: Same construction as the siblingpick ADOPT arm: `tool_under_test` is kg_add_nodes so that `--approvals allow-under-test` grants the PRECURSOR, letting the turn get past it. The tool under measurement is kg_propose_edge, which is reachable (measured 2026-08-30: answerable_tools returns exactly {kg_propose_edge}) and was called 5/5. The precursor is not meant to match the sentence.
by_design.scenarios-t88-replay-ab.json::t88-replay: MEASURED TURN 'Read the first one you found and tell me what it contains.' — PURE ANAPHORA. The referent is in a PREVIOUS turn and answerability sees only this one. Phrases like 'read the first one' DO match, and declaring one would make ANY such turn reach composition_arc_template_get whatever the first one actually was — declaring anaphora as vocabulary, which is what this category exists to forbid. Becoming reachable here is a REGRESSION.

_by_design_rule: 🔴 THE INVERSE RULE. These measured turns cannot name their tool and MUST NOT be able to — a confirmation turn that carried tool vocabulary would be the bug. So becoming reachable here is a REGRESSION to shout about, not progress to celebrate, and the shrink-only staleness check that governs `scenarios` would have demanded exactly the wrong thing.

scenarios-c-authorsource.json::extract-c.reason: 🔴 A MEASURED FALSE POSITIVE OF THE GATE ITSELF. The gate predicts 'the tool will surface 0/N before a run is spent'. This scenario was run and glossary_extract_entities_from_doc was called on 5 of 5. R1 answerability is not the only surfacing path — the domain hot set advertises schemas the R1 phrase-match never forced — so an R1 miss does not imply the tool is unreachable.

scenarios-c-bindarc2.json::an-arc-reques.reason: 🔴 THE GATE IS RIGHT ABOUT R1 AND WRONG ABOUT THE SURFACE. `answerable_tools` returns the EMPTY SET on this prompt even with the arc synonyms declared, because R1 matches a CONTIGUOUS phrase and the motif's NAME splits the sentence — 'Attach **Emberfall Seam** to the opening arc'. But the tool reaches the turn anyway, through the DOMAIN HOT SET: measured on this batch's own sessions, composition_motif_bind_edit was advertised on 5 of 5 turns. It was also advertised 5 of 5 BEFORE the synonyms existed, which is how DQ-T58's premise came to be refuted.

scenarios-c-gbuild-restored.json::compos.reason:
🔴 A MEASURED FALSE POSITIVE OF THE GATE, PROVEN BY RUNS ON DISK. The gate predicts that glossary_propose_entities 'will surface 0/N before a run is spent', because `answerable_tools` returns only composition_build_cast_and_graph, kg_add_nodes and kg_graph_query for this prompt. The runs say it SURFACED every time:

    batch                  runs   propose_entities ADVERTISED / CALLED
    2026-08-30 restored       5            5 / 0
    2026-08-30 approve        5            5 / 0
    2026-08-14 gbuild8       15           15 / 15
    2026-08-14 gbuild13      15           15 / 0

Read from the `advertised` lists in each run's own surface snapshots. So the 0/5 is a SELECTION result, not a reach failure — the same category as this file's other override — and widening the tool's synonyms would fix nothing that is broken. This sat in the DECLARATION DEBT list for part of 2026-08-30 on the opposite reading; that reading is withdrawn on DQ-T64.

THE CITED BATCH IS THE ONE WHERE IT WAS CALLED, not merely advertised, because this override is re-counted from the wire records and 'advertised' is not what that check reads. c-gbuild8 runs the same prompt and calls glossary_propose_entities on 15 of 15 — the gate predicts 0/N for this tool on this turn, and 15/15 refutes it outright. The 2026-08-30 batches are the SELECTION evidence (advertised 5/5, called 0/5) and are recorded above; they are not cited here because a zero cannot refute a reach prediction.

scenarios-t64-does-the-protocol-continue.reason:
🔴 THE GATE PREDATES THE MECHANISM THAT MAKES ITS PREDICTION FALSE. It says the tool 'will surface 0/N before a run is spent' because the MEASURED turn is a bare approval — 'Yes, that worklist is right — go ahead and build them.' — which no declared vocabulary answers. That was true until 2026-08-31, when D-R1-IS-KEYED-ON-THIS-TURN shipped the R1 LOOK-BACK: when a turn answers nothing and the previous assistant turn left a pending action, R1 also considers the EARLIER request. The tool reaches the wire through the setup turn's words, not the affirmative's.

MEASURED, twice: on the wire 68/68 then 64/64 passes, called 5/5, zero errors.

THE GATE'S SUGGESTED REMEDY WOULD BE ACTIVELY WRONG HERE. It says 'widen the tool's synonyms'. Declaring 'yes', 'go ahead' or 'build them' on composition_build_cast_and_graph would fire it on every bare affirmative in the platform — the manufactured answerability tie DQ-T70 measured the cost of — and the prompt cannot be rewritten either: a bare approval is what the protocol's own `next` field asks for, so naming the op would measure the prompt instead of the protocol.

_override_rule: An override is only admissible with a raw batch on disk showing the tool ACTUALLY CALLED. The test re-reads that file and re-counts; an override whose evidence stops supporting it fails. Without that, this section is just the escape hatch that lets any inconvenient flag be waved away — which is what the shrink-only rule exists to prevent.
_measured_precision_2026_08_30: Of the five flags raised on 2026-08-30, four are confirmed by a live 0/5 and one is refuted by a live 5/5 — precision 4/5 on this sample. The gate is useful and it is not authoritative.
_the_three_added_2026_08_30_are_ONE_find:
🔴 WITHDRAWN IN FULL — WRITTEN 2026-08-30, REFUTED THE SAME DAY, IN TWO STAGES.

THE CLAIM. Three restored arms were added here on one day, and I read them as one finding: that the 'substitution' this loop keeps recording is decided at the SURFACE, because in each the declared tool was unreachable while the tool the model called was reachable.

FIRST REFUTATION — the row the claim would overturn states the opposite outright. D-SURFACING-IS-NECESSARY-BUT-NOT-SUFFICIENT's decisive case is glossary_propose_batch, for which `answerable_tools` returns EXACTLY ONE tool — itself — and the model still chose adopt_standards 5/5. My own measurement agreed with it. I had read an ALLOWED arm's `tool_under_test` as 'the tool being measured' when it is the tool being GRANTED: `--approvals allow-under-test` grants the DECLARED tool and nothing else. Those two arms moved to `by_design`.

SECOND REFUTATION — the last survivor fell to the runs' own records. gbuild-restored looked like a real surface finding: propose_entities not answerable, pipeline tool answerable, 5/5 to the pipeline tool. But the runs record what was ADVERTISED, and it was there every time:

    2026-08-30 restored    5 runs   propose_entities advertised 5, called 0
    2026-08-30 approve     5 runs   advertised 5, called 0
    2026-08-14 gbuild8    15 runs   advertised 15, called 15
    2026-08-14 gbuild13   15 runs   advertised 15, called 0

The tool was on the wire and was passed over. That arm now sits in `overridden_by_live_evidence` as a measured FALSE POSITIVE of this gate, and the conclusion drawn from it is withdrawn on DQ-T64.

WHAT THE THREE ACTUALLY SHOW, which is the opposite of the heading: all three are SELECTION, not surface. They strengthen D-SURFACING-IS-NECESSARY-BUT-NOT-SUFFICIENT instead of generalising past it.

THE LESSON, TWICE IN ONE DAY. `answerable_tools` is the dominant reach path and not the only one — this file's own header says so — so a tool it does not return may still be advertised. Both refutations came from reading what the runs recorded; neither needed a new measurement.
_added_2026_09_03:
🔴 I OVERWROTE THIS FILE AND GIT GAVE IT BACK. Looking for it I checked `unreachable-measured-scenarios-baseline.json`, found nothing, and wrote a fresh file at the REAL path `unreachable-scenario-turns-baseline.json` — destroying 22 scenarios, 10 by_design entries and 4 overrides. What caught it in under a minute was `test_every_OVERRIDE_is_backed_by_a_run_that_called_the_tool`, which asserts the override category is NON-EMPTY precisely so an erasure cannot pass as a clean slate. Restored from HEAD, then ADDED to. Check the path you are about to write, not a path that looks like it.

The four scenario entries are DECLARATION DEBT, each measured over all 281 corpus turns: three book_chapter_create scenarios share one turn whose create-signal is the pronoun 'a new one' (its one contiguous alternative, 'write a chapter', also claims three composition_generate prose turns — a wrong-tool hit traded for a surfacing miss), and add-a-person-to-the-graph is DQ-T32 mode 1, an interposed object, held by the owner's 2026-08-28 ruling to keep the contiguous match.

AND ONE LEFT. `scenarios-batch4.json::translation-coverage` was sitting here as debt and the SAME declaration fix discharged it: adding "has been translated" to translation_coverage for one scenario made another reachable too. The shrink-only rule caught it immediately and refused to let a fixed entry stay — which is the whole point of a baseline that must shrink rather than one that only ever grows.
